defect_disposition.disposition: closed - ACCEPTED as proposed, not re-routed
defect_disposition.decision: KEEP the lettering. style.json CR-012 now names the Hatter's hat price ticket, marked 10/6, as an allowed in-world lettering.
defect_disposition.reasoning: The ticket is not a style choice, it is canon (ch011-p37; CHAR-hatter, FAC-mad-tea-party), and it is exactly the class of lettering CR-012 was written to permit: small, in-world, period hand-inked, physically motivated on a real object. CR-012 exists to keep Mucha poster typography and modern overlays out of frame, not to strip the Bible's own props and costume marks. A hand-inked price tag in a hat band is period-true under CR-002 (1862 trade practice) and carries no Art Nouveau display typography, so admitting it costs the rule nothing. Rejecting it would have deleted a canon detail to protect a whitelist, which is the wrong way round.
defect_disposition.alternative_not_taken: The alternative_if_rejected branch (drop the ticket from bible/costumes.json COS-015 and route back to memory-bible for a user ruling) was NOT taken. No costume change goes back to 06-art/costume or memory-bible for this finding.
defect_disposition.redo_cost_assessment: ZERO. No image regenerated (re-roll budget 0). COS-015 already carried the ticket as its working value, so no costume, prop or concept artefact becomes stale. No prompt-consumed field moved, so no already-written p7 prompt changes meaning and nothing must be re-emitted.

only the short price mark 10/6 need read on screen; the full phrase 'In this style 10/6' is not required
